messages:
andrew: quick follow-up from the continuation RFC thread — we need to pick a single resume/continuation token contract for Python/TS/Go SDKs. main questions: opaque vs structured, who parses/validates, and runtime retry semantics. can we decide by EOD?

sarah: +1 opaque by default. apps shouldn't need to parse tokens. SDKs can ship light helpers for debugging.

mike: opaque seems nicer for users, but we must nail transport invariants. if a transport retry replays a partial chunk we need resume token to be idempotent and verifiable.

lex: quick counterpoint: opaque tokens hide routing metadata. e.g., gateway -> edge handoff needs model/version info to pick the right backend. if opaque, the gateway either must carry extra headers or ask the origin. that adds complexity.

andrew: agreed. tradeoff list: opaque = simpler SDK surface, harder ops/debug; structured = easier routing, tighter coupling and parsing in every language. current token (what we have in prod) is basically a base64 JSON with model, seq, kv_hash.

sarah: proposal: canonical token layout = base64(JSON) with fields {v:int, model:str, offset:int, sig:str}. default SDK behavior: treat as opaque for resume semantics, but provide parse_token(token) in debug helpers to inspect/validate. transports must not rely on parsing for resume correctness.

mike: must include an HMAC(sig) over model+offset+nonce, yes. also include a monotonic nonce or epoch so old tokens can't be replayed across rollouts.

lex: transport contract we should document: 1) server returns token T_n for position n, 2) client persists last acked token, 3) on reconnect, client calls ResumeStream(ctx, token) and server must accept token iff token.sig valid and token.offset <= current stream tail. on mismatch server returns 409+expected_token.

andrew: sketch APIs so implementers have a clear surface:

Python:
```python
# sync iterator style
stream = client.resume_stream(token=T)
for chunk in stream:
    process(chunk)
# helper for debug
print(client.parse_token(T))
```

TypeScript:
```ts
// async iterator
for await (const chunk of client.stream.resume(T)) {
  handle(chunk)
}
// debug helper
console.log(client.stream.parseToken(T))
```

Go:
```go
// Resume returns a channel that yields chunks, or an error on start
ch, err := client.ResumeStream(ctx, token)
if err != nil { return err }
for c := range ch {
  handle(c)
}
// debug helper
fmt.Println(client.ParseToken(token))
```

mike: added note: transports should expose resume/backoff knobs (max_retries, max_resume_attempts, base_backoff_ms). Example config snippet:
```yaml
transport:
  max_retries: 5
  max_resume_attempts: 3
  base_backoff_ms: 200
  on_resume_failure: fallback-to-snapshot
```

lex: for cross-lang parity: keep names consistent: resume_stream / stream.resume / ResumeStream and parse_token / parseToken / ParseToken. keep the helpers hidden under "debug" flags so we don't encourage parsing in prod.

ci-bot: /note: RFC continuation-token-v2 merged to main, docs/transport/continuation.md added (link: https://git.internal/r/continuation-token-v2) :white_check_mark:

sarah: i'll write a small conformance test: start a stream, drop connection after N tokens, resume with last token, assert no duplicates and final offsets match. will share PR by EOD.

andrew: perfect. if no objections by EOD i'll send a short RFC amendment and we can land the SDK shape. :thumbsup:

mike: ack. small nit: call the field "offset" not "seq" — clearer semantics.

lex: ack. i'll update gateway routing to fetch token metadata only when header routing absent.

andrew: thanks all — keeping this tight helps implementers. if anything else, ping me directly.
